thread:
incident-bot: Pager: HIGH tail latency detected on /v1/generate (hosted-prod). 95p > 2.1s for last 5m, backlog rising. Auto-escalate to on-call.

eric: Got the page, I'm looking. seeing GPU queue length spike on shard-gw-7. latency correlates with sustained QPS bump + lower throughput on batcher.

maya: Confirming. Metrics: batch_wait_ms median jumped from 6ms -> 28ms, batch_size mean went down 22 -> 14 (we're getting smaller, more frequent batches). Could be continuous batching parameters reacting to bursty short requests.

jules: Any recent deploys?

eric: No prod deploys in last 30m. No canary. Rolling infra autoscaler did a small scale-in earlier which might have reduced concurrency headroom.

kira: Customer impact: degraded latency observed on 4 major tenants (not all). No 5xx. Streaming connections are more impacted (client-side perceived stall).

eric: First mitigation idea: move to throughput-optimized batching to clear backlog but accept higher median latency for non-interactive customers. Specifically increase continuous_batch.window_ms from 10 -> 40 and allow max_batch_size 32 -> 64 on /v1/generate route for hosted-prod. This should increase effective batch occupancy and GPU utilization.

maya: Agreed but we should also limit to non-streaming routes and apply only to default model variant. We don't want to break single-token low-latency flows like chat streaming.

jules: Proposed traffic shaping plan: 1) apply batching config change to route-id "gen-default" (non-streaming only) 2) throttle /v1/generate streaming to 60% of baseline for 10m with quota bump later if stable 3) re-route lower-priority customers to model-compact fallback.

eric: I'll make the batching change first (quick and reversible). Executing command on control plane:

```bash
# increase window and max batch size for gen-default on hosted-prod
redwoodctl routes update --env hosted-prod --route gen-default \\  --set continuous_batch.window_ms=40 \\  --set continuous_batch.max_batch_size=64
```

eric: running now. patch applied.

incident-bot: action recorded: route update submitted by eric at 1825000062.

maya: Seeing immediate change in batch occupancy — mean batch_size -> 48, batch_wait_ms -> 42ms (expected). GPU utilization rose ~12%. Throughput per GPU increased.

eric: 95p latency trend: temporarily rose from 2.1s -> 2.8s for affected non-streaming requests (expected tradeoff), but queue depth is decreasing and errors zero.

jules: Good. Now applying streaming throttle for 10m to reduce pressure on small interactive flows.

jules: Command:

```bash
redwoodctl quotas update --env hosted-prod --route gen-streaming \\  --set rate_limit.qps=0.6*baseline --duration=10m --reason "incident: reduce pressure on batcher"
```

incident-bot: quota change applied at 1825000125 by jules.

kira: Monitoring customer impact: streaming tail-latency for top tenants dropped by ~30% after throttle (less jitter); non-streaming median increased but backlog cleared.

eric: Next: re-route low-priority tenants to model-compact fallback. Will create temporary routing rule weight shift 80/20 default->compact.

eric: applying:

```bash
redwoodctl routing update --env hosted-prod --route gen-default \\  --set traffic_split.default=0.8,compact=0.2 --duration=30m --reason "mitigation: reduce pressure on default model"
```

eric: done at 1825000189.

maya: Metrics 5m after changes: overall GPU queue length down 65%; throughput stable; 95p latency trending down toward pre-incident levels for streaming; non-streaming 95p still elevated but slowly normalizing.

jules: Customer comms note: affected tenants A/B see increased median latency for bulk generate jobs; interactive chat users stable. Ops to follow up with CS to notify any tenants with SLO concerns.

eric: I'm going to keep batching window at 40ms for next 30m and watch. If stability holds, we'll try dialing window to 30ms to recover latency.

kira: Can we also enable generous client-side hints to allow longer timeouts for bulk endpoints? CC product.

jules: I will create a short runbook step for this incident: include exact commands we ran, metrics to watch (batch_wait_ms, batch_size, GPU queue length, 95p latency), and rollback steps.

eric: Handing off to ops-rotation for longer monitoring and follow-up. My pager free for next 20m.

ops-rotation: Taking over. Confirmed all mitigations in place. Will check every 5m and escalate if errors or latency worsen.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: mitigation = increased continuous_batch.window_ms, increased max_batch_size, streaming throttle, traffic-split to compact model. Start time 1825000000.

maya: Post-incident action items: - run replay of burst workload in staging with window_ms=40 to calibrate; - add per-tenant dynamic batching profile (auto-detect short-vs-bulk flows); - evaluate whether autoscaler should avoid scale-in when average batch occupancy < threshold.

jules: Agreed. I'll own runbook updates and follow-up tasks.

eric: Closing on-call handoff. leaving notes in #incidents.

ops-rotation: Last check at 1825000375: system stable, backlog drained. Will keep mitigation rules for 30m then gradually revert if steady.

incident-bot: Incident status -> mitigated (monitoring).
